guitar.guitaristsText: John Lennon / George Harrison / Paul McCartney
guitar.modelsText: Rickenbacker 325/360-12, Gretsch, Epiphone Casino, Gibson J-160E
guitar.evidence: Trained knowledge: well documented across multiple guitars and eras — Lennon's Rickenbacker 325/Casino, Harrison's Gretsch/Rickenbacker 360-12, McCartney mainly bass (Hofner) with some guitar use.
guitar.notes: Original entry reasonable as a summary across three members and many guitars; kept as-is.

tone.target: bright jangly Beatles clean with slight compression
tone.profile: bright jangly Beatles clean with slight compression
tone.summary: A classic jangly Beatles sound achieved with a Comp boost for attack, followed by the UK 45 amp model, paired with the UK Vintage 4x12 cabinet to capture the required brightness and clarity.
corrections: lean Vox chime, not Fender twin

blocks.purpose: Clean up ambient noise and hum.
Provide tight clean attack and smooth out dynamics.
Keep the tone clean and pure.
Emulate the bright, chimey sound of a Vox AC30.
blocks.gap: The UK 45 is an approximation; true Vox emulation might require specific EQ adjustments.

blocks.purpose: Provide a bright and articulate platform for the clean tone.
blocks.gap: The UK Vintage 4x12 is used for its clarity rather than specific Vox voicing.

blocks.purpose: Enhance the bright top end and jangly character.
No wah effect needed for this clean tone.
Add subtle depth without sounding distracting.
blocks.gap: A very minimal delay is used to add space, but the focus remains on dryness.

blocks.purpose: Provide a short room ambiance as requested.

improvements.summary: Improve cabinet realism and voicing for a more authentic Vox/Rickenbacker chime.

proposals.reason: The current cabinet is too generic; a dedicated Vox-style IR will enhance the chime.
